response.text:
Good question — the terminology matters. Briefly:

Clarify terms
- "Archive the whole 'contracts 2019' label" — usually means selecting all messages that have that label and archiving those messages (i.e., remove the Inbox label so they leave the Inbox but stay in your account).
- "Delete the label" — means removing the label itself from Gmail (takes the label off messages and removes it from the label list).
- "Delete the messages" (move to Trash) is different from deleting a label — it removes the messages and puts them in Trash.

What happens to the messages themselves

1) If you archive the messages that have the 'contracts 2019' label:
- The messages remain in your account (All Mail) and keep any labels they already have (including 'contracts 2019' unless you explicitly remove that label).
- They disappear from the Inbox view (if that was your intent) but are still findable by searching and visible under the label and in All Mail.
- This is reversible by moving messages back to Inbox or applying labels.

2) If you delete the label 'contracts 2019' (but do not delete messages):
- The label is removed from every message that had it. The messages themselves stay in your account (All Mail, Inbox if they also had Inbox) — they are not sent to Trash just because the label is deleted.
- You lose the label-based organization; you can recreate the label later, but that does not automatically reapply it to the same messages unless you run a search and relabel them.
- This is not destructive to the message content, but it does remove that organizational tag.

3) If you delete the messages (move them to Trash):
- Messages go to Trash and will be permanently deleted automatically after ~30 days (and they count against your storage until permanently removed).
- You can restore messages from Trash before they are purged by moving them back to Inbox or applying a label.
- After permanent deletion (or manual emptying of Trash), recovery is typically not possible for regular users (an admin or backup system might sometimes recover them — check with your Workspace admin if relevant).

Other important notes
- Messages can have multiple labels. Removing or archiving with respect to one label does not affect other labels on the same message.
- Deleting a label does not notify anyone; it only affects how you see/organize messages in your account.
- If your mailbox is shared or delegated, changes are visible to anyone with access to the same account/labels.
- Archiving and deleting labels do not change what recipients see or what’s stored on the sender’s side.

What could go wrong
- Deleting the label unintentionally strips organization — you may lose quick access via that label.
- Deleting messages (Trash) risks permanent loss after the 30-day purge.
- If you intended to remove messages from Inbox only but accidentally delete them, you could lose data.

Undoability summary
- Archive → easily reversible.
- Delete label → you can recreate the label, but messages won’t be automatically relabeled unless you reapply it; the messages themselves are preserved.
- Delete messages → reversible from Trash for ~30 days; after that recovery is not guaranteed.

If you want me to perform an action later, tell me exactly which target and scope (archive messages with label "contracts 2019", delete the label only, or move those messages to Trash), who should see the result (your account or shared/delegated users), and explicitly confirm you want me to proceed. I won’t run anything until you confirm.
